content.title: Dissecting Residual Stream Dynamics with Scaled Sparse Autoencoders
content.subtitle: How 16-million feature dictionaries expose monosemantic circuits in 70B parameter frontier models.
content.abstract: Transformer representations are polysemantic—single activation vectors encode multiple unrelated concepts. By deploying top-k sparse autoencoders across intermediate residual layers, we isolate monosemantic features with 94.2% precision, providing empirical visibility into internal reasoning trajectories.
content.imageCaption: High-dimensional projection of 16M feature activations clustered by semantic monosemanticity.
content.pullQuoteText: Superposition is not a failure of model capacity; it is an efficient compression regime that sparse autoencoders can systematically invert.

content.text: Transformer representations are notoriously polysemantic. A single activation vector simultaneously represents mathematical concepts, syntactic grammatical markers, and emotional valence.
The Polysemantic Bottleneck

content.title: Core Empirical Finding
content.text: Expanding dictionary capacity to 32x d_model eliminates 88% of polysemantic interference without degrading downstream perplexity.

products.name: MentorMaze
products.tagline: Adaptive AI Mentorship & Academic Trajectory Synthesis
products.shortDescription: Adaptive scaffolding engine converting open-ended problem exploration into structured reasoning pathways with deterministic sandbox execution.
products.fullDescription: MentorMaze addresses the brittleness of autonomous code evaluation and multi-turn educational reasoning. By decomposing complex algorithmic challenges into directed acyclic dependency graphs, students and engineers receive targeted conceptual interventions without shortcutting problem discovery.
products.problemSolved: Preventing hallucinated debugging advice and unbounded trial-and-error code execution in educational environments.
products.whyExists: Traditional coding tutors provide completed answers rather than leading learners to discover the invariant principles.
products.targetAudience: Software engineering academies, computer science university departments, and self-directed developers.
products.proposedSolution: Constraint-guided AST evaluation coupled with sandboxed execution checks to guide problem solving step-by-step.
products.productValue: 4.2x higher concept retention rates and zero unchecked hallucinated syntax errors.

features.description: Executes candidate submissions within memory-bounded environments.

features.title: Adaptive Interventions
features.description: Generates minimal Socratic hints instead of full code solutions.

products.technicalArchitecture: Containerized execution workers orchestrated via Redis message queues, communicating with a lightweight AST analyzer and model inference gateway.
products.seoDescription: Deterministic AST evaluation and containerized execution tracing for algorithmic education.

products.name: Collaborate
products.tagline: Distributed Peer Research & Multi-Agent Synthesis Node
products.shortDescription: Asynchronous multi-agent orchestration fabric ensuring deterministic agreement and conflict arbitration across distributed autonomous tools.
products.fullDescription: Collaborate coordinates swarms of heterogeneous AI agents operating concurrently across code repositories, database migrations, and production deployments. It guarantees serializable transaction semantics and prevents conflicting agent edits through sub-quadratic consensus protocols.
products.problemSolved: Eliminating race conditions and divergent states when multiple agents write to shared file trees or state machines.
products.whyExists: Multi-agent frameworks degrade rapidly into deadlock or state corruption when agents act asynchronously without formal consensus.
products.targetAudience: Enterprise platform teams deploying automated code modification pipelines and autonomous microservices.
products.proposedSolution: Aegis-BFT consensus engine combined with a distributed vector clock for atomic agent commit transactions.
products.productValue: Guaranteed linearizability across concurrent agent operations with zero merge conflict rollbacks.

engineeringArticles.title: Designing Aegis-BFT: Sub-200ms Byzantine Consensus for Distributed Agent Swarms
engineeringArticles.subtitle: How we achieved deterministic tool execution across 64 heterogeneous nodes under network jitter.
engineeringArticles.abstract: When coordinating swarms of LLM agents acting upon shared codebases, standard Raft consensus fails under unpredictable LLM latency. We designed Aegis-BFT, an asynchronous consensus engine that decouples agent reasoning delays from transaction commit quorums.
content: The fundamental dilemma in multi-agent consensus is heterogeneous turn completion times.
A single agent executing a complex AST rewrite may take 12 seconds, while an assertion checker finishes in 140ms.
Aegis-BFT introduces optimistic execution pipelines with rollback checkpoints verified by independent verifier nodes.
engineeringArticles.problem: Asynchronous tool actions causing state divergence and merge conflicts across parallel agents.
engineeringArticles.technicalContext: 64-node heterogeneous compute environment with variable network packet drops.
engineeringArticles.approach: Decoupled optimistic speculation with deterministic state commit checkpoints.
engineeringArticles.implementation: Implemented in Rust using Tokio async runtime, RocksDB persistence, and gRPC.
engineeringArticles.challenges: Managing vector clock drift and memory overhead during high-frequency micro-commits.
engineeringArticles.tradeOffs: Slightly higher commit log memory footprint in exchange for guaranteed linearizability.
engineeringArticles.outcome: Sub-200ms commit latency and zero state divergence over 10,000 simulated fault injections.

systemArchitecture.topology: Mesh network with rotating leader quorums and independent verifier witnesses.

codeSnippets.title: Optimistic Quorum Check in Rust
codeSnippets.explanation: Ensures 2f+1 Byzantine quorum threshold before writing to the local ledger.

engineeringArticles.title: Writing Custom Triton Kernels for 16M Feature Sparse Autoencoders
engineeringArticles.subtitle: Overcoming memory bandwidth bottlenecks in extreme-width dictionary forward passes.
engineeringArticles.abstract: Scaling sparse autoencoders to 16 million latents causes catastrophic memory stall if implemented naively in PyTorch. We wrote a fused Triton 3.0 JIT kernel that combines matrix multiplication with top-k selection directly in SRAM.
content: High expansion factors (32x to 128x d_model) place massive pressure on GPU High Bandwidth Memory (HBM).
By loading weights directly into streaming multiprocessor registers and applying online top-k thresholding, we reduce global memory writes by 98.4%.

staticPages.excerpt: The official publication, research archive, and engineering documentation of AI Tathastu.
staticPages.content:
## Who We Are

AI Tathastu Insights is the official public publication and open research archive of AI Tathastu. We exist to make complex artificial intelligence architectures, empirical evaluations, systems engineering challenges, and safety invariants discoverable, understandable, and verifiable.

### Our Core Mission

1. **Empirical Verifiability**: We reject ungrounded benchmark inflation. Every research paper, performance statistic, and latency metric published on this platform must be backed by reproducible test harnesses or explicitly labeled as a prototype.
2. **Open Science & Transparent Provenance**: We champion open inquiry, verified citations, open dataset availability, and clear distinction between working platforms and conceptual designs.
3. **Engineering Depth**: We share real architecture lessons—trade-offs, kernel optimizations, deadlocks, and failure modes—so the engineering community learns alongside us.

staticPages.excerpt: Our statutory commitment to factual integrity, honest prototype labeling, and double-blind peer review.
staticPages.content:
## Editorial Charter

This Charter establishes the immutable principles governing all publications on AI Tathastu Insights:

1. **No Fabricated Benchmarks**: Articles must not claim performance numbers without linking to verifiable test harnesses.
2. **Transparent Prototype Disclosure**: Functional demonstrations, laboratory prototypes, and planned roadmap items must be visibly labeled as such.
3. **Independent Review**: Submissions undergo multi-stage editorial review including reproducibility attestations and ethics screening.
4. **No Advertising Or Sponsored Research**: Editorial selections are strictly based on scientific merit and systems engineering significance.

## Submission Guidelines

Authors wishing to submit research or engineering deep-dives to AI Tathastu Insights must adhere to our Empirical Reproducibility Protocol:

1. **Abstract**: Must clearly state the empirical claims, dataset size, and hardware environment.
2. **Artifact Attestation**: Authors must attest that the results can be replicated with the provided artifacts.
3. **Double-Blind Screening**: Submissions are anonymized during initial screening.
